court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: V. Prema Kumari vs M. Palani
facts_of_case: Appellant, a minor, was kidnapped by respondent and taken to Thiruvannamalai. She was rescued and respondent claimed they were married. Appellant filed for declaration of marriage as null and void and respondent filed for restitution of conjugal rights. Trial court dismissed appellant's petition and granted respondent's petition.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage of a minor is voidable at the instance of the minor.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that under Hindu Law the marriage of the minor is a voidable marriage at the instance of the minor.

legal_principles.principle: The consent of the petitioner or guardian must be obtained without force or fraud for a marriage to be valid.
legal_principles.held: This provision is applicable if the consent of the petitioner or the consent of the guardian of the petitioner was obtained by force or fraud.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized before a person attains the age of 15 years can be repudiated after attaining that age but before attaining the age of 18 years.
legal_principles.held: To attract this provision the marriage should have been solemnised before she attained the age of 15 years and she has to repudiate the marriage after attaining that age but before attaining the age of 18 years.

outcome.final_order: Appellate court set aside trial court order and declared marriage null and void, and also ordered respondent to pay costs.

use_for_drafting: responding to nullity of marriage claim
